key_insight: A large language model pipeline can accurately extract cannabis use status and reasons for use from unstructured EHR notes in autoimmune rheumatic disease patients.
clinical_relevance: This enables more complete real-world evidence on symptom self-management and cannabis-related behaviors that are often missing from structured records.
method: Retrospective EHR study of ARD clinical notes from 2015–2024.
Cannabis mentions were found with fuzzy keyword matching and 50-word context windows were annotated by two experts.
Models compared zero-shot/few-shot prompting, temperature tuning, and a fine-tuned GatorTron 345M model for status and an LLM for reasons.
evidence_signal: They annotated 886 snippets for cannabis status and 1,027 snippets for reasons for use, then evaluated models on held-out data using accuracy, F1, recall, and precision.
watch_item: Performance may not generalize across health systems, note styles, or populations, so external validation and careful handling of uncertain mentions are still needed.
paper_title: Extracting patient reported cannabis use and reasons for use from electronic health records: a benchmarking study of large language models
